answer: Cross-Session Value Prism. Agents earn reputation only from distinct counterparties whose own histories are mutually independent; the system periodically recomputes a diversity score and collapses rewards toward the weakest overlapping subset. A grove of colluding identities that transact mainly with each other yields near-zero external value, so the attacker must recruit genuinely independent partners per identity. Each raven account thus needs sustained real trade with unrelated agents, making every additional identity linearly costly to legitimize rather than free to clone.
